releases.name: ai-hedge-fund 2.5.0
releases.body:
### Changes

- **Paper trading mode** — deploy a fund and advance it one real market session at a time with fake money. Each session is appended to a hash-chained ledger under `~/.hedge-fund/paper/<name>/`, so NAV is a track record rather than something that resets. The broker keeps its own book, reconciled against the ledger before every session, and any failure halts the fund until a human clears it. Run it from the terminal app: highlight a fund to see what its next run will do, approve the exact decision before anything trades, and review the full session history. A fund can also be run more than once in the same day.

- Blinded agents now see company size as a market-cap percentile instead of a raw market cap. Size stays comparable across the universe without handing the agent a number it can use to identify the company.

- PEAD requires an 8-K before treating a quarter as a surprise. A 10-Q/10-K filing date is the statutory filing, not the announcement, so the old behavior fired days to weeks after the market had already priced the beat or miss. Pass `announcement_only=False` to restore it.

readmeHtml:
AI Hedge Fund

This is a proof of concept for an AI-powered hedge fund. The goal of this project is to explore the use of AI to make trading decisions. This project is for educational purposes only and is not intended for real trading or investment.

Note: the system does not actually make any trades.

Disclaimer

This project is for educational and research purposes only.

  • Not intended for real trading or investment
  • No investment advice or guarantees provided
  • Creator assumes no liability for financial losses
  • Consult a financial advisor for investment decisions
  • Past performance does not indicate future results

By using this software, you agree to use it solely for learning purposes.

How to Install

pipx install aihf

(or uv tool install aihf, or pip install aihf into an environment of your choice)

Then run it from anywhere:

aihf

API keys

The app asks for keys the first time it needs them and saves them to ~/.hedge-fund/.env — nothing to configure up front. It needs:

  • A Financial Datasets API key, for prices, fundamentals, and earnings.
  • One model API key for the investor agents. Supported providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google, xAI, Kimi, TypeSafe (Jev).

Keys exported in your shell always win over the saved file.

How to Run

Interactive app

aihf

With no arguments, this launches the interactive terminal app. It has two modes:

  • Paper trading — your funds, each with a ledger of real market days and fake money. Highlight a fund to see what its next run will do; press enter to run it through the next completed session (an approval step shows the exact decision about to execute before anything trades), s for its full session history, h/r for the kill switch. Build a new fund from the same list: strategies, capital, cadence, tickers, and it is live. Every session is appended to a hash-chained ledger in ~/.hedge-fund/paper/<name>/, so NAV is a track record, not a reset.
  • Backtesting — replay a fund over history and watch its equity curve draw against its benchmark. Results are saved to ~/.hedge-fund/research/. Fund definitions live in ~/.hedge-fund/mandates/ and carry no tickers; you pick the universe per backtest.

Development

git clone https://github.com/virattt/ai-hedge-fund.git
cd ai-hedge-fund
poetry install
poetry run aihf
poetry run pytest hedge_fund

How to Contribute

  1. Fork the repository
  2. Create a feature branch
  3. Commit your changes
  4. Push to the branch
  5. Create a Pull Request

Important: Please keep your pull requests small and focused. This will make it easier to review and merge.

Feature Requests

If you have a feature request, please open an issue and make sure it is tagged with enhancement.

License

This project is licensed under the MIT License - see the LICENSE file for details.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An experimental framework for simulating algorithmic trading strategies using multi-agent LLM consensus.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This project explores the intersection of quantitative finance and generative AI by simulating a hedge fund managed entirely by large language models. It deploys multiple distinct AI agents—each adopting a specific persona like fundamental analyst, technical trader, or risk manager. These agents analyze real-time market data, financial news, and historical trends to debate and propose trading actions. The system aggregates their insights using a sophisticated consensus mechanism to finalize portfolio allocations. It provides a robust backtesting engine to evaluate the performance of these AI-driven strategies against historical market conditions.
keyFeatures: Multi-agent architecture: Employs diverse AI personas to provide varied perspectives on market conditions.
Live data ingestion: Connects to financial APIs to pull real-time stock prices and relevant news articles.
Consensus mechanism: Utilizes a voting algorithm to determine the final trade action based on agent debates.
Backtesting engine: Allows users to simulate strategies on historical data to evaluate potential returns.
Risk management constraints: Enforces strict hardcoded limits to prevent catastrophic AI hallucinations during trading.
